passage:
"You laughed so loudly when you fell!" Darshan said, dropping onto the canteen bench beside Urmila. "You looked so confident."
"Confident?" She stared at him. "Darshan, I wanted the floor to swallow me. Forty people watched me trip on my own bag strap."
"But you got up, took a bow and everyone clapped."
"That's because I laughed first. If I hadn't, I think I'd have run out." She rubbed her elbow. "It was half funny, half horrible."
"I honestly thought you didn't care."
"I care about everything. That's the problem."
Darshan grinned and pushed his fries toward her. "Next time, I'll sit close. Deal?" She took one. "Deal."

qa.a: She tripped on her own bag strap.

qa.q: What was Urmila feeling as she laughed loudly?
qa.a: She was embarrassed and afraid of looking foolish, and the laugh helped cover it and gave her relief, though part of it was truly funny.

qa.q: What could Darshan do next time a friend slips in public?
qa.a: He could stay close and check in afterwards, because a big laugh may be covering embarrassment rather than showing confidence.

qa.q: How did the onlookers likely read Urmila's laughter?
qa.a: They read it as confidence and clapped, so they missed how uncomfortable she felt.

grounding: A teen laughs loudly after a slip in front of others to cover embarrassment, and others read it as confidence.

passage: In Class 11 I once walked into the glass door of the physics lab in front of everyone. It made an actual thud. I remember the exact second: silence, then my own voice booming with laughter before anyone else's. I even said "Ta-da!" and waved. People cheered. Francis, who sat next to me, gave me a thumbs up and told me afterwards I was the most relaxed person he'd ever seen. I nodded as though I was. But my ears were burning, and I went to the toilets and stood there for five minutes, hands under cold water, feeling foolish and relieved at the same time. I still laugh first when I slip. I just know now what that laugh is. - Samir

qa.q: What did Samir walk into in front of everyone?
qa.a: Samir walked into the glass door of the physics lab.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling while standing in the toilets?
qa.a: Samir felt foolish and relieved, since the loud laugh had covered the embarrassment and the room had accepted it.

qa.q: What could Samir tell Francis in order to be understood?
qa.a: Samir could say that the laugh was covering embarrassment and that the relaxed look was not the whole story.

qa.q: How did Francis see Samir after the slip?
qa.a: He saw a very relaxed person, so he misread the laugh as confidence.

grounding: A teen laughs loudly after a slip to cover embarrassment, others read it as confidence, and the laugh may be relief.
